finalText:
Redis died at 2:14am, and everything downstream fell apart from there.

At 02:14:07 the app lost its connection to Redis (`ECONNREFUSED` on `10.0.0.12:6379`). It fell back to hitting the database directly, which it couldn't keep up with. Every request started timing out after 5 seconds, and the backlog of waiting requests kept growing.

For the next 17 minutes it tried to reconnect to Redis every couple minutes and failed each time, 12 attempts in a row, while the request queue climbed past 500 and worker memory filled up. At 02:31:44 worker-2 ran out of memory and crashed. Eight seconds later the whole API stopped responding and the supervisor killed it, at 02:31:52.

So the trigger was Redis going down. The crash itself was caused by requests piling up faster than they could drain once caching was gone. Worth checking why `10.0.0.12:6379` was unreachable, and adding a queue limit or circuit breaker so a dead cache can't take the whole API down next time.
